subject: fix: Flatpak signing key (#1745)
body:
## What?

Adds signing to flatpak

## Why?

Fixes #1710

Signed-off-by: drew <me@andrinoff.com>
diff:
diff --git a/.github/workflows/static.yml b/.github/workflows/static.yml
index 87ef36e..5db0155 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/static.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/static.yml
@@ -40,10 +40,22 @@ jobs:
           sudo apt-get install -y flatpak flatpak-builder
           flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo
 
+      - name: Import Flatpak signing key
+        env:
+          FLATPAK_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.FLATPAK_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          export GNUPGHOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/gnupg"
+          mkdir -m 700 "$GNUPGHOME"
+          echo "$FLATPAK_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" | gpg --batch --import
+          KEY_ID=$(gpg --list-secret-keys --with-colons | awk -F: '/^fpr/ {print $10; exit}')
+          echo "GNUPGHOME=$GNUPGHOME" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          echo "KEY_ID=$KEY_ID" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          echo "GPGKey=$(gpg --export "$KEY_ID" | base64 -w0)" >> public/matcha.flatpakref
+
       - name: Build Flatpak Repo
         run: |
-          flatpak-builder --user --install-deps-from=flathub --repo=public/repo --force-clean build-dir com.floatpane.matcha.yaml
-          flatpak build-update-repo --generate-static-deltas public/repo
+          flatpak-builder --user --install-deps-from=flathub --gpg-sign="$KEY_ID" --gpg-homedir="$GNUPGHOME" --repo=public/repo --force-clean build-dir com.floatpane.matcha.yaml
+          flatpak build-update-repo --gpg-sign="$KEY_ID" --gpg-homedir="$GNUPGHOME" --generate-static-deltas public/repo
 
       - name: Setup Pages
         uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

author: OG Green
subject: fix(i18n): arabic dual vs 3-10 plurals (#1732)
body:
## What?

Arabic relative times (`time.minute_ago`, `hour_ago`, `day_ago`,
`week_ago`, `month_ago`, `year_ago`, `in_minute`, `in_hour`, `in_day`):
the dual text ("منذ يومين" / "two days ago") was stored under `few`.
This moves it to `two` and puts the 3–10 plural in `few` (دقائق، ساعات،
أيام، أسابيع، أشهر، سنوات).

## Why?

`ArabicPlural` maps 2 → `two` and 3–10 → `few`, so in the inbox list a
message from 5 days ago showed "منذ يومين" (two days ago), and one from
2 days ago fell through to `other` ("منذ 2 يوم"). Rendered through `Tn`
with `ar`:

| n | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | منذ 2 يوم | منذ يومين |
| 3 | منذ يومين | منذ 3 أيام |
| 10 | منذ يومين | منذ 10 أيام |
| 11 | منذ 11 يوماً | منذ 11 يوماً |

`go test ./i18n/...` passes. A native speaker's look at the `few`
wording would be welcome.

+## Help bars show your keys
+
+Every bottom help bar is rendered from the active `keybinds.json`, so a remapped binding shows up in the help text after the next restart. Remap `email.reply` to `q` and the email view prints `q: reply` instead of `r: reply`.
+
+Arrow keys stay printed next to remapped navigation (`↑/↓/p/n`) because they always work, and translated help strings are built from the same bindings, so non-English users see their own keys too.
+
+Two places still document the built-in keys, because those handlers don't read config yet: the settings panes and the modal pickers (file picker, login, password prompt).
+

diff --git a/tui/keybind_help.go b/tui/keybind_help.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2608937
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tui/keybind_help.go
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+package tui
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/floatpane/matcha/config"
+	"github.com/floatpane/matcha/i18n"
+)
+
+// helpSeparator joins the fragments of every bottom help bar.
+const helpSeparator = " • "
+
+// kbKey returns the configured key for an action. Remapped keys are shown and
+// matched identically; an empty entry falls back to the built-in default so a
+// help bar never renders a blank key.
+func kbKey(key, def string) string {
+	if strings.TrimSpace(key) == "" {
+		return def
+	}
+	return key
+}
+
+// helpEntry is a single "icon key: description" fragment of a help bar.
+type helpEntry struct {
+	icon string
+	key  string
+	desc string
+}
+
+// helpItem builds one help fragment. Pass an empty icon for fragments without
+// a nerd-font glyph.
+func helpItem(icon, key, desc string) helpEntry {
+	return helpEntry{icon: icon, key: key, desc: desc}
+}
+
+func (e helpEntry) String() string {
+	fragment := e.key + ": " + e.desc
+	if e.icon != "" {
+		fragment = e.icon + " " + fragment
+	}
+	return fragment
+}
+
+// joinHelp renders help fragments as one bullet separated line.
+func joinHelp(entries ...helpEntry) string {
+	fragments := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
+	for _, entry := range entries {
+		fragments = append(fragments, entry.String())
+	}
+	return strings.Join(fragments, helpSeparator)
+}
+
+// joinKeys merges key labels into one slash separated label, dropping empty
+// and repeated entries so an unremapped binding keeps its original wording.
+func joinKeys(keys ...string) string {
+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(keys))
+	unique := make([]string, 0, len(keys))
+	for _, key := range keys {
+		if key == "" || seen[key] {
+			continue
+		}
+		seen[key] = true
+		unique = append(unique, key)
+	}
+	return strings.Join(unique, "/")
+}
+
+// navArrowsLabel describes up/down navigation. Arrow keys always work, so the
+// default binding reads "↑/↓"; remapped keys are appended, e.g. "↑/↓/p/n".
+func navArrowsLabel() string {
+	kb := config.Keybinds
+	up := kbKey(kb.Global.NavUp, "k")
+	down := kbKey(kb.Global.NavDown, "j")
+	if up == "k" && down == "j" {
+		return "↑/↓"
+	}
+	return joinKeys("↑", "↓", up, down)
+}
+
+// navVimLabel describes up/down navigation by the configured keys themselves,
+// matching the "j/k" wording used by the folder overlays.
+func navVimLabel() string {
+	kb := config.Keybinds
+	return joinKeys(kbKey(kb.Global.NavDown, "j"), kbKey(kb.Global.NavUp, "k"))
+}
+
+// cancelKey returns the configured cancel/back key, used by help bars in every
+// view that routes back navigation through the global bindings.
+func cancelKey() string {
+	return kbKey(config.Keybinds.Global.Cancel, "esc")
+}
+
+// keybindHelpData exposes the active keybinds as template variables, letting
+// translated help strings show the user's own keys instead of the defaults.
+func keybindHelpData() map[string]interface{} {
+	kb := config.Keybinds
+	return map[string]interface{}{
+		"NavArrows":   navArrowsLabel(),
+		"NavVim":      navVimLabel(),
+		"Cancel":      kbKey(kb.Global.Cancel, "esc"),
+		"Quit":        kbKey(kb.Global.Quit, "ctrl+c"),
+		"NextField":   kbKey(kb.Composer.NextField, "tab"),
+		"PrevField":   kbKey(kb.Composer.PrevField, "shift+tab"),
+		"Editor":      kbKey(kb.Composer.ExternalEditor, "ctrl+e"),
+		"UndoSend":    kbKey(kb.Composer.UndoSend, "u"),
+		"NextFolder":  kbKey(kb.Folder.NextFolder, "tab"),
+		"PrevFolder":  kbKey(kb.Folder.PrevFolder, "shift+tab"),
+		"Move":        kbKey(kb.Folder.Move, "m"),
+		"FocusFolder": joinKeys(kbKey(kb.Folder.FocusPreview, "]"), kbKey(kb.Folder.FocusInbox, "[")),
+	}
+}
+
+// keybindHelp resolves a help string through i18n (plugin overrides included) and
+// fills its {Placeholder} slots with the active keybinds.
+func keybindHelp(key string) string {
+	return i18n.NewTemplate(t(key)).Execute(keybindHelpData())
+}
diff --git a/tui/keybind_help_test.go b/tui/keybind_help_test.go

+package tui
+
+import (
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/floatpane/matcha/config"
+)
+
+// setKeybinds installs a modified copy of the active keybind config for the
+// duration of a test and restores it afterwards.
+func setKeybinds(t *testing.T, customize func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig)) {
+	t.Helper()
+	previous := config.Keybinds
+	t.Cleanup(func() { config.Keybinds = previous })
+
+	kb := previous
+	customize(&kb)
+	config.Keybinds = kb
+}
+
+func TestEmailHelpShowsCustomKeys(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig) {
+		kb.Email.Reply = "q"
+		kb.Email.Delete = "x"
+		kb.Email.FocusAttachments = "g"
+		kb.Global.Cancel = "ctrl+g"
+	})
+
+	help := (&EmailView{}).renderHelp()
+	for _, want := range []string{"q: reply", "x: delete", "g: focus attachments", "ctrl+g: back to inbox"} {
+		if !strings.Contains(help, want) {
+			t.Errorf("email help missing %q, got %q", want, help)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, unwanted := range []string{"\uf112 r:", "\uea81 d:", "\uf435 tab:", "\ueb06 esc:"} {
+		if strings.Contains(help, unwanted) {
+			t.Errorf("email help still shows default %q, got %q", unwanted, help)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestEmailAttachmentHelpShowsCustomKeys(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig) {
+		kb.Global.NavUp = "p"
+		kb.Global.NavDown = "n"
+	})
+
+	m := &EmailView{focusOnAttachments: true}
+	help := m.renderHelp()
+	if !strings.Contains(help, "↑/↓/p/n: navigate") {
+		t.Errorf("attachment help missing remapped navigation, got %q", help)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestEmailHelpKeepsDefaultWording(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(_ *config.KeybindsConfig) {})
+
+	help := (&EmailView{}).renderHelp()
+	want := "\uf112 r: reply • \uf064 shift+r: reply all • \uf064 f: forward • \uea81 d: delete • \uea98 a: archive • \uf435 tab: focus attachments • \ueb06 esc: back to inbox"
+	if !strings.Contains(help, want) {
+		t.Errorf("default email help changed shape:\ngot:  %q\nwant: %q", help, want)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDraftsHelpShowsCustomKeys(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig) {
+		kb.Drafts.Open = "o"
+		kb.Drafts.Delete = "shift+d"
+	})
+
+	bindings := NewDrafts(nil).list.AdditionalShortHelpKeys()
+	got := make([]string, 0, len(bindings))
+	for _, b := range bindings {
+		got = append(got, b.Help().Key+": "+b.Help().Desc)
+	}
+	joined := strings.Join(got, " • ")
+	if !strings.Contains(joined, "\ue5fe o: open") || !strings.Contains(joined, "\uea81 shift+d: delete") {
+		t.Errorf("drafts help missing custom keys, got %q", joined)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestFolderHelpShowsCustomKeys(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig) {
+		kb.Folder.NextFolder = "ctrl+f"
+		kb.Folder.PrevFolder = "ctrl+b"
+	})
+
+	m := &FolderInbox{inbox: &Inbox{}}
+	m.updateHelpKeys()
+	if len(m.inbox.extraShortHelpKeys) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("expected 2 folder help keys, got %d", len(m.inbox.extraShortHelpKeys))
+	}
+	first := m.inbox.extraShortHelpKeys[0]
+	if first.Help().Key != "ctrl+f" || !slices.Contains(first.Keys(), "ctrl+f") {
+		t.Errorf("next folder help key = %q, want the configured binding", first.Help().Key)
+	}
+	if second := m.inbox.extraShortHelpKeys[1]; second.Help().Key != "ctrl+b" {
+		t.Errorf("prev folder help key = %q, want %q", second.Help().Key, "ctrl+b")
+	}
+}
+
+func TestKeybindHelpFillsTranslatedPlaceholders(t *testing.T) {
+	setKeybinds(t, func(kb *config.KeybindsConfig) {
+		kb.Composer.NextField = "ctrl+j"
+		kb.Composer.PrevField = "ctrl+k"
+		kb.Global.Cancel = "ctrl+g"
+	})
+
+	help := keybindHelp("composer.help")
+	if !strings.Contains(help, "ctrl+j/ctrl+k: navigate") || !strings.Contains(help, "ctrl+g: save draft & exit") {
+		t.Errorf("composer help missing custom keys, got %q", help)
+	}
+	if strings.Contains(help, "tab/shift+tab") || strings.Contains(help, "{") {
+		t.Errorf("composer help shows defaults or unfilled placeholders: %q", help)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestJoinKeysDropsDuplicates(t *testing.T) {
+	if got := joinKeys("↑", "↓", "↑"); got != "↑/↓" {
+		t.Errorf("joinKeys dedup = %q, want %q", got, "↑/↓")
+	}
+	if got := joinKeys("a", "", "a", "b"); got != "a/b" {
+		t.Errorf("joinKeys = %q, want %q", got, "a/b")
+	}
+}

subject: feat(i18n): complete Spanish (#1733)
body:
## What?

Closes #1507.

The existing `es.json` was missing 9 keys that exist in `en.json`. This
PR translates all 9:

| Key | Translation |
|-----|-------------|
| `choice.mouse_help` | Pulsa y para activar o n para desactivar... |
| `choice.mouse_prompt` | ¿Activar soporte para ratón? [s/n] |
| `common.logs` | Registros |
| `common.no_logs_yet` | Sin registros todavía |
| `composer.encrypt_pgp` | Cifrar correo (PGP) |
| `composer.sign_pgp` | Firmar correo (PGP) |
| `composer.sign_smime` | Firmar correo (S/MIME) |
| `settings_general.mouse_support` | Soporte para ratón |
| `settings_general.show_original_on_reply` | Mostrar original al
responder |

## Why?

An incomplete locale leaves Spanish-speaking users with untranslated
English strings mixed into the UI. With this change the Spanish locale
reaches **234/234 keys — 100% coverage**, matching `en.json`
key-for-key.

Translations follow the existing style in `es.json`. Technical terms
(PGP, S/MIME) kept as-is. `s/n` used instead of `y/n` for yes/no prompts
in Spanish.

Co-authored-by: Eddy-AliceLabs <eddyflores100-lang@users.noreply.github.com>

index 0000000..325ebe0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/scripts/demo-sandbox.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Builds a throwaway $HOME with a Maildir account full of fake mail for
+# demo.tape, so the README GIF never touches a real inbox.
+# Usage: .github/workflows/scripts/demo-sandbox.sh [sandbox_dir]
+# (default sandbox_dir: <repo>/.demo-sandbox, which demo.tape expects)
+# Set MATCHA_BIN to use a prebuilt binary instead of building this checkout.
+# Works on macOS and Linux (needs python3 for portable date handling).
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
+SANDBOX="${1:-$ROOT/.demo-sandbox}"
+rm -rf "$SANDBOX"
+
+# Build matcha from this checkout and put a quiet wrapper on the sandbox PATH
+# (stderr logging would otherwise bleed into the recorded TUI).
+mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/bin"
+if [[ -n "${MATCHA_BIN:-}" ]]; then
+  cp "$MATCHA_BIN" "$SANDBOX/bin/matcha-bin"
+else
+  (cd "$ROOT" && go build -o "$SANDBOX/bin/matcha-bin" . 2>/dev/null)
+fi
+cat > "$SANDBOX/bin/matcha" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/sh
+exec "$(dirname "$0")/matcha-bin" "$@" 2>/dev/null
+SH
+chmod +x "$SANDBOX/bin/matcha"
+
+MAIL="$SANDBOX/Mail/demo"
+mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/.config/matcha" "$SANDBOX/.cache/matcha"
+for d in "" .Sent .Archive; do mkdir -p "$MAIL/$d/cur" "$MAIL/$d/new" "$MAIL/$d/tmp"; done
+
+cat > "$SANDBOX/.config/matcha/config.json" <<JSON
+{
+  "accounts": [
+    {
+      "id": "demo",
+      "name": "Ada Lovelace",
+      "email": "ada@matcha.email",
+      "service_provider": "custom",
+      "protocol": "maildir",
+      "maildir_path": "$MAIL"
+    }
+  ],
+  "disable_daemon": true,
+  "disable_notifications": true,
+  "hide_tips": true,
+  "has_seen_setup_guide": true,
+  "enable_split_pane": true,
+  "theme": "Matcha"
+}
+JSON
+
+# Skip the one-time matcha: URL handler registration; it talks to the
+# system-wide LaunchServices database, which a sandbox must not touch.
+touch "$SANDBOX/.config/matcha/.protocol_registered"
+
+n=0
+# msg <folder> <flags> <from> <subject> <minutes_ago> <body...>
+msg() {
+  local folder="$1" flags="$2" from="$3" subject="$4" ago="$5"; shift 5
+  n=$((n + 1))
+  local ts=$(( $(date +%s) - ago * 60 ))
+  local date; date=$(python3 -c 'import sys, email.utils; print(email.utils.formatdate(int(sys.argv[1]), localtime=True))' "$ts")
+  local dir="$MAIL/$folder/cur"
+  local file="$dir/${ts}.demo${n}.matcha:2,${flags}"
+  {
+    printf 'From: %s\nTo: Ada Lovelace <ada@matcha.email>\nSubject: %s\nDate: %s\n' "$from" "$subject" "$date"
+    printf 'Message-ID: <demo%d@matcha.email>\nMIME-Version: 1.0\nContent-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8\n\n' "$n"
+    printf '%s\n' "$@"
+  } > "$file"
+  python3 -c 'import os, sys; t = int(sys.argv[2]); os.utime(sys.argv[1], (t, t))' "$file" "$ts"
+}
+
+msg "" "" "Grace Hopper <grace@compiler.dev>" "Launch checklist for v1.0 🚀" 4 \
+  "Hey Ada," "" \
+  "We're nearly there. Before we tag v1.0 tomorrow:" "" \
+  "  1. Final pass on the release notes" \
+  "  2. Smoke-test the Homebrew + Nix installs" \
+  "  3. Record the demo video (the fun part)" "" \
+  "Ping me once the build is green and I'll hit publish." "" "— Grace"
+msg "" "" "GitHub <noreply@github.com>" "[floatpane/matcha] PR #1720: Add threaded view" 18 \
+  "linus-t requested your review on this pull request." "" \
+  "  + Group conversations by Message-ID / References" \
+  "  + Collapse and expand threads with T" "" \
+  "View it on GitHub."
+msg "" "S" "Alan Turing <alan@bletchley.org>" "Re: Lunch on Thursday?" 55 \
+  "Thursday works. The usual place at 12:30?" "" "Alan"
+msg "" "" "Linear <notifications@linear.app>" "MAT-212 moved to In Review" 90 \
+  "Ada Lovelace moved MAT-212 \"Inline image previews\" to In Review."
+msg "" "S" "Margaret Hamilton <margaret@apollo.space>" "Design review notes" 180 \
+  "Thanks for the walkthrough today. Main takeaways:" "" \
+  "  - Keyboard-first everything" \
+  "  - Zero mouse required, but nice when it's there" \
+  "  - Ship themes, people love themes" "" "M."
+msg "" "S" "Stripe <receipts@stripe.com>" "Your receipt from Floatpane #2041-1188" 300 \
+  "Amount paid: \$12.00" "Thanks for supporting open source."
+msg "" "S" "Dennis Ritchie <dmr@bell-labs.com>" "Re: K&R second edition" 600 \
+  "Happy to send you a signed copy. Still the best way to learn C."
+msg "" "S" "Hacker Newsletter <hi@hackernewsletter.com>" "#712: terminals are cool again" 1500 \
+  "This week: TUIs, Bubble Tea, and why your inbox belongs in a terminal."
+msg "" "S" "Ken Thompson <ken@plan9.org>" "UTF-8, napkin edition" 2900 \
+  "Sketched it on a placemat at dinner. Scan attached in spirit."
+msg "" "S" "Barbara Liskov <barbara@mit.edu>" "Substitution principle talk" 4400 \
+  "Slides are up. Let me know if you want the speaker notes too."
+msg ".Sent" "S" "Ada Lovelace <ada@matcha.email>" "Re: Design review notes" 170 \
+  "Agreed on all three. Themes are already in."
+msg ".Archive" "S" "Charles Babbage <charles@engine.co>" "Difference Engine invoice" 9000 \
+  "Attached is the final invoice for the analytical bits."
+
+echo "$SANDBOX"

author: KAWACU Kennedy
subject: fix: cache inline image payloads (#1707)
body:
## What?

Inline `cid:` images never render. `CachedAttachment` stored only
attachment metadata, so the decoded payload of inline attachments was
dropped on cache write and never restored on cache read.
`inlineImagesFromAttachments` skips attachments with empty `Data`, so
the CID lookup always resolved against an empty map.

This PR adds a `Data []byte` field to `CachedAttachment` and:
- persists the decoded payload for inline attachments via
`cachedAttachmentToConfig` (the single cache-write path in
`app/app.go`),
- restores it via `cachedAttachmentsToFetcher` (the single cache-read
path, used by both the preview and full-body cache hits),
- counts it in `calculateEmailBodySize` so LRU accounting stays
accurate.

## Why?

Fixes #1702. With the payload cached, the CID lookup in
`ProcessBodyWithInline` resolves and inline images render via the Kitty
graphics protocol like remote ones.

subject: fix(imap): oauth2 url fix for outlook (#1701)
body:
## What?

- Added try-catch block to make it easier to debug OAuth2 errors
encountered while authenticating IMAP.
- Revised Outlook URL generation code for updated Entra ID redirect

## Why?

I wasn't able to authenticate my Outlook emails previously. I'm not
fully sure if the documentation clearly states that you need your Entra
ID redirect to be configured as "Web" rather than "Mobile & Desktop
App," but that is also a needed fix.

subject: fix(config): better config parse errors (#1691)
body:
## What?

Wrap config file parse errors with the file path, and replace the
`panic()` in `defaultKeybinds()` with a logged warning.

## Why?

Closes #1520

When a config file is malformed, the error only showed a raw JSON parse
error with no indication of which file was broken. Users had no way to
know what to fix.

If the embedded `default_keybinds.json` was somehow corrupted, the
application crashed with a panic instead of degrading gracefully.

---------

author: Drew Smirnoff
subject: fix: daemon socket death (#1648)
body:
## What?

Fixes 2 bugs causing connection close and daemon socket death.

1. Added a `call()`  wrapper around all `daemonService` methods that:

* Detects connection-level errors via `isConnError()`
* Closes the dead client and calls `tryConnectWithConfig()` to reconnect
(auto-starts
daemon if needed)
* Retries the operation once on the fresh connection

2. Added `closeMu sync.Mutex` to serialize the `close(done)` operation
between `Close()` and `readLoop()`.

## Why?

When socket died, matcha became unusable for 5-10 minutes

---------

Signed-off-by: drew <me@andrinoff.com>

subject: docs: changelog stale-queued reaper entry
diff:
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 53b0499..6fd9a09 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -16,6 +16,13 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
   `Retry-After` header (seconds). Checks are serialized per tenant via a
   Postgres advisory lock and fail open when the quota path errors.
   Disable with `QUOTAS_ENABLED=false`.
+- Stale-queued reaper: when a JetStream message is dropped (e.g.
+  `MaxDeliver` exceeded) but the row stays `queued`, the dispatcher's
+  reaper sweep now marks it `failed` with reason `stale_queued` after
+  `STALE_QUEUED_AFTER` (default `10m`, must exceed `AckWait 90s` ×
+  `MaxDeliver 5`; set `0` to disable). Counted as `failed` for quota
+  purposes, so a poison submit no longer permanently consumes a free
+  tier's active cap with a misleading `429`.
 
 ## [0.1.1] - 2026-09-12

 ## Security model
 
-- **Sandbox** — per-execution container: gVisor runtime, UID/GID 65534,
-  `NetworkMode: none`, read-only rootfs with writable tmpfs `/tmp` and
-  `/work`, `cap-drop: ALL`, 128 MB RAM (+128 MB swap), 0.5 CPU, 32 pids.
-  Code and stdin arrive as a tar over the container's stdin (no bind
-  mounts, so it works identically from inside or outside Docker).
-  Stdout/stderr are truncated at 64 KiB each. OOM kills are detected and
-  reported as failures.
-- **Tenancy** — users ↔ tenants is many-to-many via `memberships`; the
-  middleware re-checks membership per request (a stale token can't reach
-  a tenant you've left). Cross-tenant reads return `404`, never leak.
-- **Webhooks** — `webhook_url` must be http(s) on a public host (DNS
-  re-resolved at delivery; `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` lifts this for local
-  dev). Deliveries are HMAC-SHA256-signed over `<timestamp>.<body>`,
-  retried 3× on transport errors/5xx/429, never follow redirects.

+- **Webhooks** — public http(s) only (`WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` lifts for dev),
+  HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>`, 3× retry, no redirects.

subject: feat(install): add multi-client installer and vaults-sync skill
body:
Adds skills/vaults-sync/SKILL.md, a workflow skill agents load mid-session when the user asks to save, write, sync, or structure notes (or types /vault-sync). Teaches vault resolution, read-before-write with expected_sha256, operation choice, frontmatter, wiki-link and tag conventions, and ADR / runbook / spec skeletons; links to the existing skills/vaults-hub tool reference instead of duplicating it.

Adds install.sh: dry-run-by-default POSIX bash installer that detects OpenCode, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Codex CLI. For each detected client it merges the vaults MCP entry into the right config (mcp.servers.vaults for OpenCode, mcpServers for Claude/Cursor, [mcp_servers.vaults] TOML for Codex), symlinks vaults-sync into ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills, and drops a short auto-load AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md hint. Refuses piped execution, merges JSON via jq with a python3 + comment-stripping JSONC fallback so opencode.jsonc is handled without clobbering user comments, never overwrites an existing vaults entry with a different value, and writes the new value atomically via tmp+mv.

README gains an 'Install via your AI agent' section with a copy-paste prompt for AI assistants and a corrected mcp.servers.vaults example. CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased].

Signed-off-by: Ishaan Jindal <ishaanjindal2006@gmail.com>

+
+The script detects which MCP clients you have installed (OpenCode,
+Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex), registers the `vaults`
+MCP server in each, symlinks the `vaults-sync` skill into the global
+skills directory, and drops a short `AGENTS.md` hint so every session

+
+To run it yourself (clone first so you can inspect):

+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/ishaan-jindal/vaults-hub.git
+cd vaults-hub
+./install.sh --help        # see what it will do
+./install.sh --apply       # actually write configs

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# install.sh - register the `vaults` MCP server and the `vaults-sync` skill with
+# every supported MCP client installed on this machine.
+#
+# Dry-run by default; pass --apply to actually write:
+#   ./install.sh            # show what would happen
+#   ./install.sh --apply    # merge configs, symlink the skill, drop hints
+set -eu
+
+# --- guards ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Piped execution means nobody read this script before running it.
+if [ -z "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" ] || [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = /dev/stdin ]; then
+  printf '%s\n' 'refuse to run from pipe; download and inspect first' >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+REPO_ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)
+SKILL_SRC="$REPO_ROOT/skills/vaults-sync"
+
+usage() {
+  printf '%s\n' \
+    'usage: install.sh [--apply]' \
+    '' \
+    'Detect installed MCP clients (OpenCode, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor,' \
+    'Codex CLI). For each one: register the `vaults` MCP server, symlink the' \
+    'vaults-sync skill into the shared skill dirs, and drop an auto-load hint.' \
+    '' \
+    'Default is a dry run: nothing is written. Pass --apply to apply.' >&2
+}
+
+apply=0
+for arg in "$@"; do
+  case "$arg" in
+    --apply) apply=1 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) printf 'unknown argument: %s\n' "$arg" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [ ! -d "$SKILL_SRC" ]; then
+  printf 'skill source not found: %s\n' "$SKILL_SRC" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+warn() { printf 'WARNING: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+
+rows=()
+add_row() { rows+=("$(printf '%-18s %s' "$1" "$2")"); }
+
+HINT_BODY='# vaults-hub MCP
+
+The `vaults` MCP server is registered. When the user asks to save, sync, write, or structure notes, load the `vaults-sync` skill before acting.'
+
+# Drop the hint into an existing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, or create a 5-line one.
+# Appends rather than clobbering a user-authored config-root file.
+ensure_hint() {
+  hint_file=$1
+  if [ -f "$hint_file" ] && grep -qF '# vaults-hub MCP' "$hint_file"; then
+    say "  ok: auto-load hint already in $hint_file"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if [ "$apply" != 1 ]; then
+    say "  would add auto-load hint to $hint_file"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$hint_file")"
+  wrote=0
+  if [ -f "$hint_file" ]; then
+    { cat "$hint_file"; printf '\n%s\n' "$HINT_BODY"; } > "$hint_file.tmp" && wrote=1
+  else
+    printf '%s\n' "$HINT_BODY" > "$hint_file.tmp" && wrote=1
+  fi
+  if [ "$wrote" = 1 ] && mv "$hint_file.tmp" "$hint_file"; then
+    say "  auto-load hint written to $hint_file"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  rm -f "$hint_file.tmp"
+  warn "$hint_file: could not write auto-load hint"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Symlink the skill dir into a client skills dir. Sets LINK_STATE for the summary.
+ensure_link() {
+  link_dest=$1
+  if [ -L "$link_dest" ]; then
+    link_now=$(readlink "$link_dest")
+    if [ "$link_now" = "$SKILL_SRC" ]; then
+      LINK_STATE='already linked'
+      say "  ok: $link_dest -> $SKILL_SRC"
+    else
+      LINK_STATE='conflict'
+      warn "$link_dest points to $link_now, not $SKILL_SRC - leaving it untouched"
+      return 1
+    fi
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if [ -e "$link_dest" ]; then
+    LINK_STATE='conflict'
+    warn "$link_dest exists and is not a symlink - leaving it untouched"
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [ "$apply" != 1 ]; then
+    LINK_STATE='would link'
+    say "  would link $link_dest -> $SKILL_SRC"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if mkdir -p "$(dirname "$link_dest")" && ln -s "$SKILL_SRC" "$link_dest"; then
+    LINK_STATE='linked'
+    say "  linked $link_dest -> $SKILL_SRC"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  LINK_STATE='failed'
+  warn "$link_dest: could not create symlink"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Strip // line comments and trailing commas from a .jsonc stream so jq/python3
+# can parse it. Writes cleaned JSON to stdout. Used only when the config file
+# ends in .jsonc; .json files pass through unchanged.
+jsonc_stdin() {
+  python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
+import re, sys
+path = sys.argv[1]
+with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+    raw = handle.read()
+# Drop // line comments that are not inside a string. Conservative: skip
+# strings first, strip comments outside them, then reassemble. JSONC has
+# no block comments per the OpenCode / VS Code spec we follow.
+def strip(line):
+    out, i, in_str, esc = [], 0, False, False
+    while i < len(line):
+        ch = line[i]
+        if in_str:
+            out.append(ch)
+            if esc:
+                esc = False
+            elif ch == "\\":
+                esc = True
+            elif ch == '"':
+                in_str = False
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        if ch == '"':
+            in_str = True
+            out.append(ch)
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == "/":
+            break
+        out.append(ch)
+        i += 1
+    return "".join(out)
+cleaned = "\n".join(strip(ln) for ln in raw.splitlines())
+# Remove trailing commas before } or ].
+cleaned = re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", cleaned)
+sys.stdout.write(cleaned)
+PY
+}
+
+# Merge the `vaults` entry into a JSON config without touching anything else.
+# $1 = file, $2 = shape: "opencode" (.mcp.servers.vaults) or "mcpServers".
+ensure_json() {
+  json_file=$1
+  shape=$2
+  case "$shape" in
+    opencode)
+      json_key='mcp'
+      json_subkey='servers'
+      json_entry='{"type":"local","command":"npx","args":["-y","vaults-hub"]}'
+      ;;
+    *)
+      json_key='mcpServers'
+      json_subkey=''
+      json_entry='{"command":"npx","args":["-y","vaults-hub"]}'
+      ;;
+  esac
+
+  is_jsonc=0
+  case "$json_file" in
+    *.jsonc) is_jsonc=1 ;;
+  esac
+
+  # jq path expression to the vaults entry: mcp.servers.vaults vs mcpServers.vaults.
+  if [ -n "$json_subkey" ]; then
+    jq_path=".$json_key.$json_subkey.vaults"
+  else
+    jq_path=".$json_key.vaults"
+  fi
+
+  merged=''
+  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    if [ -s "$json_file" ]; then
+      if [ "$is_jsonc" = 1 ]; then
+        if jsonc_stdin "$json_file" | jq -e "$jq_path == $json_entry" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          say "  ok: vaults already registered in $json_file"
+          return 0
+        fi
+        if jsonc_stdin "$json_file" | jq -e "$jq_path != null" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          warn "$json_file: $jq_path already present (different value) - skipping to avoid duplicate"
+          return 1
+        fi
+        if ! merged=$(jsonc_stdin "$json_file" | jq ".$json_key.$json_subkey.vaults = $json_entry" 2>/dev/null); then
+          warn "$json_file: not valid JSONC (or not an object) - skipping"
+          return 1
+        fi
+      else
+        if jq -e "$jq_path == $json_entry" "$json_file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          say "  ok: vaults already registered in $json_file"
+          return 0
+        fi
+        if jq -e "$jq_path != null" "$json_file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          warn "$json_file: $jq_path already present (different value) - skipping to avoid duplicate"
+          return 1
+        fi
+        if ! merged=$(jq ".$json_key.vaults = $json_entry" "$json_file" 2>/dev/null); then
+          warn "$json_file: not valid JSON (or not an object) - skipping"
+          return 1
+        fi
+      fi
+    else
+      if [ -n "$json_subkey" ]; then
+        merged=$(printf '{}\n' | jq ".$json_key.$json_subkey.vaults = $json_entry")
+      else
+        merged=$(printf '{}\n' | jq ".$json_key.vaults = $json_entry")
+      fi
+    fi
+  elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    json_rc=0
+    merged=$(python3 - "$json_file" "$shape" "$is_jsonc" "$json_subkey" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+
+path, shape, is_jsonc, subkey = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] == "1", sys.argv[4]
+if shape == "opencode":
+    key, entry = "mcp", {"type": "local", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "vaults-hub"]}
+else:
+    key, entry = "mcpServers", {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "vaults-hub"]}
+
+try:
+    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        raw = handle.read()
+except FileNotFoundError:
+    raw = ""
+
+if is_jsonc and raw:
+    def strip_comments(line):
+        out, i, in_str, esc = [], 0, False, False
+        while i < len(line):
+            ch = line[i]
+            if in_str:
+                out.append(ch)
+                if esc:
+                    esc = False
+                elif ch == "\\":
+                    esc = True
+                elif ch == '"':
+                    in_str = False
+                i += 1
+                continue
+            if ch == '"':
+                in_str = True
+                out.append(ch)
+                i += 1
+                continue
+            if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == "/":
+                break
+            out.append(ch)
+            i += 1
+        return "".join(out)
+    raw = "\n".join(strip_comments(ln) for ln in raw.splitlines())
+    raw = re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", raw)
+
+if not raw.strip():
+    doc = {}
+else:
+    try:
+        doc = json.loads(raw)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print("WARNING: %s: unreadable JSON (%s) - skipping" % (path, exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+if not isinstance(doc, dict):
+    print("WARNING: %s: top-level JSON is not an object - skipping" % path, file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+container = doc.setdefault(key, {})
+if subkey:
+    if not isinstance(container, dict):
+        print("WARNING: %s: %s is not an object - skipping" % (path, key), file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+    container = container.setdefault(subkey, {})
+if not isinstance(container, dict):
+    print("WARNING: %s: container is not an object - skipping" % path, file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+if container.get("vaults") == entry:
+    sys.exit(3)
+if "vaults" in container:
+    print("WARNING: %s: vaults entry already present (different shape) - skipping to avoid duplicate" % path, file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(2)
+container["vaults"] = entry
+if is_jsonc:
+    print("NOTE: %s is JSONC; the merged output is JSON (comments stripped)." % path, file=sys.stderr)
+print(json.dumps(doc, indent=2))
+PY
+    ) || json_rc=$?
+    if [ "$json_rc" -eq 3 ]; then
+      say "  ok: vaults already registered in $json_file"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [ "$json_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
+      return 1 # python already warned on stderr
+    fi
+    if [ "$json_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+      return 1 # python already warned on stderr
+    fi
+  else
+    warn "neither jq nor python3 available - cannot edit $json_file"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  if [ -z "$merged" ]; then
+    warn "$json_file: empty or unparsable JSON - skipping"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  if [ "$apply" != 1 ]; then
+    say "  would register vaults in $json_file"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$json_file")"
+  # ponytail: no .bak snapshot - tmp+mv is atomic already; add copies if users
+  # need local rollback.
+  # ponytail: no post-validate of $merged - jq/python output is valid JSON by
+  # construction; re-parse if these filters ever get hand-edited.
+  if printf '%s\n' "$merged" > "$json_file.tmp" && mv "$json_file.tmp" "$json_file"; then
+    say "  registered vaults in $json_file"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  rm -f "$json_file.tmp"
+  warn "$json_file: write failed - skipping"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Record a client row and count it as a failure when its config was skipped.
+finish_client() {
+  client_name=$1
+  client_ok=$2
+  client_note=${3:-}
+  if [ "$client_ok" != 1 ]; then
+    add_row "$client_name" 'skipped (bad config)'
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+    return 0
+  fi
+  status='ok'
+  [ -n "$client_note" ] && status="ok ($client_note)"
+  [ "$apply" = 1 ] || status="$status (dry run)"
+  add_row "$client_name" "$status"
+}
+
+# --- clients ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+do_opencode() {
+  opencode_dir="$HOME/.config/opencode"
+  if [ ! -d "$opencode_dir" ]; then add_row opencode 'not detected'; return 0; fi
+  detected=$((detected + 1))
+  say ''
+  say "OpenCode: $opencode_dir"
+  opencode_cfg="$opencode_dir/opencode.json"
+  if [ ! -f "$opencode_cfg" ] && [ -f "$opencode_dir/opencode.jsonc" ]; then
+    opencode_cfg="$opencode_dir/opencode.jsonc"
+  fi
+  opencode_ok=1
+  ensure_json "$opencode_cfg" opencode || opencode_ok=0
+  ensure_hint "$opencode_dir/AGENTS.md" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+  need_agents_skills=1
+  finish_client opencode "$opencode_ok"
+}
+
+do_claude_code() {
+  claude_dir="$HOME/.claude"
+  if [ ! -d "$claude_dir" ]; then add_row 'claude-code' 'not detected'; return 0; fi
+  detected=$((detected + 1))
+  say ''
+  say "Claude Code: $claude_dir"
+  claude_ok=1
+  ensure_json "$claude_dir/settings.json" mcpServers || claude_ok=0
+  ensure_hint "$claude_dir/CLAUDE.md" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+  need_claude_skills=1
+  finish_client 'claude-code' "$claude_ok"
+}
+
+do_claude_desktop() {
+  if [ "$(uname -s)" = 'Darwin' ]; then
+    desktop_dir="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Claude"
+  else
+    desktop_dir="$HOME/.config/Claude"
+  fi
+  if [ ! -d "$desktop_dir" ]; then add_row 'claude-desktop' 'not detected'; return 0; fi
+  detected=$((detected + 1))
+  say ''
+  say "Claude Desktop: $desktop_dir"
+  warn 'Claude Desktop MCP config is unofficial; path or format may change'
+  desktop_ok=1
+  ensure_json "$desktop_dir/claude_desktop_config.json" mcpServers || desktop_ok=0
+  say '  Claude Desktop has no skills or AGENTS.md mechanism - config only'
+  finish_client 'claude-desktop' "$desktop_ok" 'unofficial'
+}
+
+do_cursor() {
+  cursor_dir="$HOME/.cursor"
+  if [ ! -d "$cursor_dir" ]; then add_row cursor 'not detected'; return 0; fi
+  detected=$((detected + 1))
+  say ''
+  say "Cursor: $cursor_dir"
+  cursor_ok=1
+  ensure_json "$cursor_dir/mcp.json" mcpServers || cursor_ok=0
+  ensure_hint "$cursor_dir/AGENTS.md" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+  need_agents_skills=1
+  finish_client cursor "$cursor_ok"
+}
+
+do_codex() {
+  codex_dir="$HOME/.codex"
+  if [ ! -d "$codex_dir" ]; then add_row 'codex' 'not detected'; return 0; fi
+  detected=$((detected + 1))
+  say ''
+  say "Codex CLI: $codex_dir"
+  codex_cfg="$codex_dir/config.toml"
+  toml_block='[mcp_servers.vaults]
+command="npx"
+args=["-y","vaults-hub"]'
+  codex_ok=1
+  if [ ! -e "$codex_cfg" ]; then
+    if [ "$apply" = 1 ]; then
+      mkdir -p "$codex_dir"
+      if printf '%s\n' "$toml_block" > "$codex_cfg.tmp" && mv "$codex_cfg.tmp" "$codex_cfg"; then
+        say "  created $codex_cfg with [mcp_servers.vaults]"
+      else
+        rm -f "$codex_cfg.tmp"
+        warn "$codex_cfg: write failed - skipping"
+        codex_ok=0
+      fi
+    else
+      say "  would register vaults in $codex_cfg"
+    fi
+  elif [ ! -r "$codex_cfg" ]; then
+    warn "$codex_cfg: not readable - skipping"
+    codex_ok=0
+  elif grep -q '^\[mcp_servers\.vaults\]' "$codex_cfg"; then
+    say "  ok: [mcp_servers.vaults] already present in $codex_cfg"
+  elif [ "$apply" = 1 ]; then
+    if { cat "$codex_cfg"; printf '\n%s\n' "$toml_block"; } > "$codex_cfg.tmp" \
+      && mv "$codex_cfg.tmp" "$codex_cfg"; then
+      say "  appended [mcp_servers.vaults] to $codex_cfg"
+    else
+      rm -f "$codex_cfg.tmp"
+      warn "$codex_cfg: write failed - skipping"
+      codex_ok=0
+    fi
+  else
+    say "  would append [mcp_servers.vaults] to $codex_cfg"
+  fi
+  ensure_hint "$codex_dir/AGENTS.md" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+  need_agents_skills=1
+  finish_client codex "$codex_ok"
+}
+
+# --- main ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+main() {
+  failures=0
+  detected=0
+  need_agents_skills=0
+  need_claude_skills=0
+
+  if [ "$apply" = 1 ]; then
+    say 'vaults-hub installer: APPLY'
+  else
+    say 'vaults-hub installer: DRY RUN (nothing will be written; pass --apply to write)'
+  fi
+  say "repo: $REPO_ROOT"
+
+  do_opencode
+  do_claude_code
+  do_claude_desktop
+  do_cursor
+  do_codex
+
+  # ~/.agents/skills serves OpenCode, Cursor and Codex; ~/.claude/skills is
+  # Claude Code's. Claude Desktop has no skills system.
+  if [ "$need_agents_skills" = 1 ]; then
+    ensure_link "$HOME/.agents/skills/vaults-sync" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+    add_row '~/.agents/skills' "$LINK_STATE"
+  fi
+  if [ "$need_claude_skills" = 1 ]; then
+    ensure_link "$HOME/.claude/skills/vaults-sync" || failures=$((failures + 1))
+    add_row '~/.claude/skills' "$LINK_STATE"
+  fi
+
+  say ''
+  say 'summary:'
+  for row in "${rows[@]}"; do
+    printf '%s\n' "$row" >&2
+  done
+
+  if [ "$detected" = 0 ]; then
+    say 'no supported MCP clients detected - nothing to do'
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if [ "$failures" != 0 ]; then
+    say "$failures problem(s); see warnings above"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  say 'done'
+}
+
+main

+---
+name: vaults-sync
+description: Turns conversation output into durable, structured vault notes — resolving the right vault, surveying and reading existing notes, then writing/append/move with optimistic concurrency and frontmatter. Use when the user asks to save, write, sync, or structure notes, document something, put content in their vault, or types /vault-sync.
+metadata:
+  version: "0.2.1"
+  mcp-server: vaults-hub
+---
+
+# Vaults Sync
+
+Workflow for persisting knowledge into `~/.vaults` via the `vaults` MCP server.
+Tool reference (arguments, returns, edge cases): see `skills/vaults-hub/SKILL.md`; do not duplicate it here.
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. **Resolve the vault.** `list_vaults`. Match by cwd basename, then git remote repo name. No match → `create_vault(name=<project-name>)`. Vault name must equal the project identity, not the topic.
+2. **Survey before writing.** `list_notes(vault=..., path="", recursive=True)` to see the existing tree; `search_notes(query=<topic>, vault=...)` to find related notes. Reuse an existing note over creating a near-duplicate.
+3. **Read before write — every time.** Any note you intend to touch gets `read_note` first and you capture `sha256`. Never self-hash; never overwrite without passing that sha back.
+4. **Choose the operation:**
+   | Situation | Call |
+   |-----------|------|
+   | New concept / new topic | `write_note` to a new path |
+   | Extending an existing note | `append_note` with `expected_sha256` |
+   | Renaming / re-homing | `move_note` (needs `src_path`, `dst_path`, `expected_sha256`) |
+5. **After writing**, re-`read_note` and confirm the returned `sha256` matches the mutation's response.
+
+```python
+vaults = list_vaults()
+notes = list_notes(vault="myproj", path="", recursive=True)
+existing = read_note(vault="myproj", path="runbooks/deploy.md")   # keep existing["sha256"]
+w = append_note(vault="myproj", path="runbooks/deploy.md",
+                content="\n## Rollback\n...", expected_sha256=existing["sha256"])
+check = read_note(vault="myproj", path="runbooks/deploy.md")       # check["sha256"] == w["sha256"]
+```
+## Frontmatter
+
+Every new note that warrants discoverability gets:
+
+```markdown
+---
+title: <human title>
+tags: [<project>/<topic>, <project>/<status>]
+created: YYYY-MM-DD
+updated: YYYY-MM-DD
+---
+```
+
+`updated` auto-refreshes only if the block already exists — set it on creation, never hand-set it on later writes.
+
+## Wiki-links and tags
+
+- Cross-reference in-vault with name-based `[[Note Name]]`. Use path-based `[[dir/Note]]` only on name collision. Never `[[../Outside]]` — the vault is the boundary.
+- Tags follow `<project-name>/<topic>` (e.g. `vaults-hub/runbook`). Run `list_tags(vault=...)` before inventing new ones and reuse what fits.
+## Note templates
+
+```markdown
+# ADR — adr-<NNNN>-<slug>.md
+## Context
+## Decision
+## Consequences
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+# Runbook — how-to-<slug>.md
+## When to use
+## Prerequisites
+## Steps
+## Verify
+## Rollback
+
+# Spec — spec-<slug>.md
+## Purpose
+## Interface   (inputs, outputs, errors)
+## Behavior    (happy path, edge cases)
+## Open questions
+```
+## Failure handling
+
+- `commit_error` in a mutation response: the disk write succeeded. Do not retry. Report the write and surface the error verbatim.
+- Sha mismatch on the post-write read: investigate with `history(vault, path)`, then `restore(vault, path, rev=...)` to roll back.
+- Numbered steps are repeatable; skipping step 3 is the #1 mistake — read first, never self-hash.

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+name: vaults-hub
+description: Manages project knowledge-base notes in Obsidian Markdown vaults (~/.vaults) via the vaults-hub MCP server. Use when reading, writing, appending, moving, deleting, searching, tagging, or restoring vault notes, frontmatter, wiki-links, and backlinks.
+metadata:
+  version: "0.2.1"
+  mcp-server: vaults-hub
+---
+
+# Vaults Hub
+
+Manages Obsidian-style Markdown vaults under `VAULTS_ROOT` (default `~/.vaults`).
+
+## Tools
+
+| Tool | Purpose |
+|------|---------|
+| `list_vaults` | List all vaults + note counts |
+| `create_vault` | Create a new vault |
+| `delete_vault` | Delete vault; requires `confirm==name`, irreversible |
+| `list_notes` | Browse notes; `path` (''=root), `recursive`, `offset`/`limit` → `total`/`truncated`/`next_offset`; `dirs=[]` when `recursive=True` |
+| `read_note` | Read note → `frontmatter`, `content`, `sha256`, `links`, `backlinks`, `unresolved_links` |
+| `write_note` | Create/update note; `expected_sha256` for guarded write |
+| `append_note` | Append text; `expected_sha256` for guarded write |
+| `delete_note` | Delete note; unguarded, no sha required; `missing_ok=True` to skip if absent |
+| `move_note` | Move/rename; args `src_path`, `dst_path`, `expected_sha256`; copy+delete, not atomic, errors if dst exists |
+| `history` | List revisions → `[{sha,date,message}]`, truncated; `untracked` if uncommitted; omit `path` for whole vault; no `rev` param |
+| `restore` | Restore `path` to git `rev` (sha from `history`); optional `expected_sha256` |
+| `list_tags` | List tags with counts; `vault` optional (omit = all vaults) |
+| `search_notes` | Full-text search; `regex`, `case_sensitive`, `limit`, `before`/`after`; `vault` optional (omit = all vaults) |
+| `server_info` | Diagnostic only (version, roots, paths) |
+
+## Happy path
+
+```python
+notes = list_notes(vault="myproj", path="", recursive=True)
+note = read_note(vault="myproj", path="todo.md")  # save note["sha256"]
+w = write_note(vault="myproj", path="todo.md", content="...", expected_sha256=note["sha256"])
+h = history(vault="myproj", path="todo.md")
+restore(vault="myproj", path="todo.md", rev=h["history"][0]["sha"], expected_sha256=w["sha256"])
+search_notes(query="todo", vault="myproj", regex=False)
+```
+
+## Rules
+
+- Paths vault-root-relative (''=root), never absolute, no escaping symlinks. Every note path arg must end in `.md` (`move_note` takes `src_path`/`dst_path`).
+- Optimistic concurrency: pass `expected_sha256` on existing notes for write/append/move/restore using `sha256` from latest read or mutation (never self-hash; `updated` auto-refresh + CRLF change bytes). Omit `expected_sha256` only when creating new note or restoring deleted note.
+- Versioning: mutations return versioning `ok`/`external`/`disabled`/`missing` + optional `commit_error`. `commit_error` means disk write succeeded — do NOT retry `append_note`. `history` returns `untracked:true` with empty list if uncommitted; raises `ValueError` if `VAULTS_HUB_GIT=0`.
+- Search: `regex=True` avoid lookarounds/backrefs (rg Rust vs Python `re`). Capped 20 hits/file, `limit` ≤200, `truncated` flag. Skips dotfiles/`.obsidian/`/`.trash/`/symlinks.
+- Frontmatter `title`/`tags`/`created`/`updated` YYYY-MM-DD; `updated` auto-refreshes only if block exists. Name-based `[[wiki-links]]`.
+- Vault name = cwd basename or git repo name; `create_vault` first if unknown (mutations raise unknown vault). Resolve vault each call.

+# TermChat UML Diagrams
+
+Source: `termchat` vault (21 notes): `01-Overview/Architecture.md`, `01-Overview/Repository-Map.md`, `04-Development/Delivery-and-Deploy.md`, `04-Development/Server-Internals.md`, `04-Development/Concurrency.md` + live code map.

+
+## 1. Package diagram
+
+```mermaid
+packageDiagram
+package termchat {
+  package shared {
+    + protocol.go : Message, Reaction, UserInfo, RoomInfo
+    + room.go : GenerateRoomCode, NormalizeRoomCode
+    + validation.go : IsValidNickname, IsValidRoomCode
+    + media.go : EncodeMediaFrame, ParseMediaFrame

+  package cli <<main>> {
+    + main.go, app.go, tui.go
+    + websocket.go, media.go
+    + lan.go, discover.go
+    + audio.go, video.go
+    + config.go, theme.go, commands.go
+  }
+  package "server/cmd/server" <<main>> {
+    + main.go
+  }
+}
+"server/cmd/server" --> server : imports
+server --> shared : imports
+cli --> shared : imports
+cli ..> server : test-only
+note right of shared : leaf, no internal imports
+```
+
+Deps are acyclic: `cmd/server -> server -> shared`, `cli -> shared`.
+
+## 2. Component diagram
+
+```mermaid
+componentDiagram
+component [CLI Binary\ncli/main] as CLI
+component [TUI\ntui, app, commands] as TUI
+component [WS Conn\nwebsocket, discover] as CONN
+component [Media AV\nmedia, audio, video] as AV
+component [LAN Beacon\nlan 224.0.0.167:9999] as LAN
+component [Server Binary\nserver/cmd/server] as SRV
+component [HTTP Mux\n9 routes] as MUX
+component [Room Registry\nroom.go + roomsMutex] as ROOMS
+component [WS Hub\nreadPump/writePump] as HUB
+component [Media Hub\nmedia.go relay] as MHUB
+component [Bootstrap\nembed sh/ps1 + /bin] as BOOT
+component [Shared Kernel\nprotocol + validation] as SHARED
+component [Caddy\nreverse_proxy :8080] as CADDY
+
+TUI -- CONN : drives
+CONN -- AV : /vc token
+LAN -- CONN : peer list
+CLI -- TUI : contains
+CLI -- CONN : contains
+CLI -- AV : contains
+CLI -- LAN : contains
+CONN --> MUX : GET /ws, /discover
+AV --> MUX : WS /media
+MUX -- HUB : upgrade
+MUX -- MHUB : dial
+MUX -- BOOT : /{room}, /bin/*
+HUB -- ROOMS : get-or-create
+MHUB -- ROOMS : peers-only relay
+SRV -- MUX : contains
+SRV -- ROOMS : contains
+SRV -- HUB : contains
+SRV -- MHUB : contains
+SRV -- BOOT : contains
+CLI ..> SHARED : GenerateRoomCode, Message
+SRV ..> SHARED : Message, RoomInfo
+CADDY --> SRV : websocket:8080
+```
+
+Interfaces: `/ws` chat, `/media` voice/video (6-byte framed PCM+JPEG), `/discover` ONLINE ROOMS, `/{room}` + `/bin/{binary}` bootstrap.
+
+## 3. Deployment diagram
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph GH[GitHub]
+    TAG[tag cli-v*] --> CLIW[cli.yml\n7 binaries + checksums\nldflags Version + DefaultWS]
+    CLIW --> REL[Release\nbinaries + termchat-checksums.txt]
+    CLIW --> AURW[aur.yml\nAUR sync via SSH]
+    CLIW --> WSIMG[websocket.yml\nGHCR termchat-websocket:tag/latest/sha]
+    CLIW --> NPMW[npm.yml OIDC as cli.yml\n8x @sacredcat/termchat*]
+    CI[ci.yml + gate.yml\ntody/gofmt/vet + race + fuzz] -. gate .-> TAG
+  end
+  subgraph VPS[VPS termchat.sacred99.online]
+    CADDY[Caddy :80/:443\nCaddyfile reverse_proxy]
+    WSC[websocket container\ndebian nonroot 10001 :8080\nWS_HOST WS_PORT\nPUBLIC_BASE_URL GITHUB_REPO]
+    WT[watchtower --interval 30]
+    CADDY --> WSC
+    WT -. pull :latest .-> WSC
+  end
+  WSIMG --> WSC
+  subgraph USER[User machine Linux/macOS/Win]
+    CURL[curl BASE_URL/room | sh\nbootstrap.sh/ps1\nRoom BaseURL Version]
+    BIN[~/.termchat cache\ntermchat-os-arch\n--server wss://.../ws]
+    TUI2[CLI TUI + LAN UDP 224.0.0.167:9999]
+    CURL --> BIN --> TUI2
+  end
+  WSC -. renders .-> CURL
+  TUI2 --> CADDY
+  REL -. fallback download .-> CURL
+  NPMW -. npm i -g .-> BIN
+```
+
+Ports/env: `WS_PORT 8080`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` drives `--server` + `/bin` redirect, `/healthz` check, idle 30m / rate 5/s enforced server-side.
